topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the key learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss traditional cancer treatment modalities along with their mechanisms of action, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: They explain therapeutic strategies that selectively exploit inherent biological defects in cancer cells, including receptor dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeting Oncogenic Kinases and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They focus on the design of small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver kinases and the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They examine targeted therapies that use engineered antibodies and antibody-toxin conjugates directed against tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explore strategies for harnessing the immune system against tumors through immune checkpoint inhibition, bispecific engagers, and cellular therapies.

topics.label: Challenges, Clinical Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the overarching challenges, historical improvements in survival, and future perspectives in the clinical management of cancer.
